subject: Post-demo: ACME throughput & budget check — batching/concurrency details
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-demo recap & next steps — throughput, batch assumptions, budget

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for hopping on the call earlier — good discussion. Quick recap and the items we promised to follow up on(see bold):

1) Target workload summary (what you said on call)
   - Peak concurrent users: ~120–160 (short spikes to 220 during batch jobs)
   - Average request size (generation): ~420 tokens; 95p generation length ~1,800 tokens
   - Embedding requests for search: ~25% of total token volume, average 128 tokens

2) Batching & concurrency expectations (we discussed continuous batching)
   - You expect streaming responses for UI flows; tail latency <= 1.2s is important.
   - Continuous batching model makes sense: steady stream of small requests from UI + periodic large inference jobs overnight.

3) Budget and unit economics (you mentioned a rough annual target)
   - Stated budget range: $60k–$120k / month initially (you said flexible in Q1)
   - Goal: keep production cost around $700 / 1M generated tokens (target we heard) — open to tradeoffs on latency vs cost.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Jordan: produce a short costing model showing $/1M token bands with batching assumptions and concurrency profiles (attached) — EOD Tue (2026-08-10).
- Dev (cc): confirm any model constraints for streaming & KV cache behavior that would change the unit econ.
- Sofia: share the procurement contact + confirmation of target monthly spend band.

Attaching a first-pass spreadsheet with throughput and token-profile inputs (redwood_throughput_assumptions_v2.xlsx) and a sanitized token profile you can review (acme_maup_token_profile.csv).

If anything above is off, call it out and I’ll adjust before we share with procurement.

Best,

Hi Sofia — looping in Rishi (pricing) and Marissa (solutions) for the budget/discount framing. A few technical assumptions I used in the attached model that materially change $/1M tokens: 

- Continuous batching behavior: for UI traffic we can leverage micro-batching with target batch size of 32–64 tokens per step given the 420-token average, which reduces amortized kernel overhead. For long-generation tails (1,800 tokens) we switch to chunked streaming which keeps latency bounded while still batching the token work across requests.
- KV cache assumptions: ~30–40% KV-hit for repeat interactive sessions (we profiled similar customers). When hits are present, effective compute per request drops ~20–30%, which reduces $/1M by a noticeable amount.
- Concurrency profile used in model: baseline 80–120 concurrent, 95p spikes 200–220. We run a continuous batching service with an adaptive max batch timeout of 20–40ms to keep UI tail latency low.

Attached I exported a scenario called "ACME-growth-95p" into the spreadsheet. The quick numbers:
- Baseline scenario (no commit, conservative batching): ~$1,050 / 1M tokens
- Continuous-batching + 30% KV hits (expected): ~$720 / 1M tokens
- Committed 12mo + optimized quantization & batching: ~$480 / 1M tokens

These are model outputs — Rishi can confirm discounting bands and any contractual framing. Let us know if you want us to prioritize a low-tail-latency variant (favoring latency over cost) vs. a cost-minimized variant.

Thanks,

Hi Sofia — quick commercial framing from our side: 

- Pricing bands we recommend (high level):
  • Entry (monthly < $40k): list pricing, limited batching optimizations
  • Growth ($40k–$120k): standard discounts, recommended continuous-batching profile modeled above
  • Committed (12mo+): deeper discounts and committed throughput reservations — we can get to the $400–$550 / 1M tokens range with commitment + quantization allowances.

- For procurement: we will provide a one-page quote + the model workbook. The workbook will include the three scenarios Dev outlined and an appendix showing sensitivity to KV cache hit rate, avg request length, and peak concurrency.

Next steps (commercial):
- Rishi: prepare one-page quote + 12mo committed discount scenarios (deliver by EOD Wed 2026-08-12).
- Sofia / Procurement: confirm the forecast band for next 12 months (needed for discounting).

If approved, Marissa can run a short POC alignment with your infra team to validate the continuous-batching runtime behavior against your peak reindex jobs.
